question: Should OpenClaw core accept model-elected continuation tools and cross-session delegate returns as an opt-in first-party agent lifecycle feature?
rationale: The PR creates new config, protocol, plugin SDK, persisted state, session lifecycle, and security-boundary behavior, so automation cannot decide whether this belongs in core or what proof bar maintainers require.

options.title: Require proof and owner approval
options.body: Keep the feature direction open but require conflict repair, maintainer product/security approval, and exact-head live receipts for continuation, delegate return, request_compaction success, and upgrade behavior before landing.

options.title: Accept experimental opt-in risk
options.body: Merge the current default-off design after maintainers explicitly own the remaining upgrade, session-state, and trusted-return boundary risk.

options.title: Split the feature
options.body: Pause this PR and ask for smaller owner-reviewed PRs that separate config/schema, continuation tools, delegate routing, compaction behavior, and proof artifacts.

recommendation.title: Require proof and owner approval
recommendation.body: Keep the feature direction open but require conflict repair, maintainer product/security approval, and exact-head live receipts for continuation, delegate return, request_compaction success, and upgrade behavior before landing.

likelyOwner.reason: The current-main history most strongly connects this owner to the central subagent lifecycle and session surfaces affected by the product decision.
